headlines.title: T-Mobile leak reveals major phone plan change for core customers
headlines.summary: T-Mobile’s latest move comes as it faces mounting pressure to keep a key part of its wireless business competitive.

headlines.title: AT&T vs. T-Mobile: Higher Dividend Yield or Faster Income Growth
headlines.summary: One telecom pays nearly double the yield and has frozen its check for years. The other pays less but keeps raising it at a double-digit clip. For retirees choosing between them, the safer bet may not be the one with the bigger payout today.

headlines.title: Starlink Spectrum Approval Could Be A Game Changer For T Mobile Stock
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US recently activated its Formula 1 regional partnership at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, using more than 20 5G-connected devices, a private 5G network, network slicing and a Smart Operations Command Center to support event operations, fan experience and broadcast production.

headlines.title: Can T Mobile US (TMUS) Turn AI Network Upgrades Into A Real Edge?
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US (NasdaqGS:TMUS) announced new AI-powered AutoPilot and Dynamic CX tools for its 5G network across the United States. The AI systems are intended to adjust network performance automatically in real time in response to shifting user demand and traffic patterns. The carrier also outlined expanded investment in backup power and diversified transport links to support service continuity during outages and emergencies.

headlines.title: T Mobile US (TMUS) Shows Off F1 5G Push On An Undervalued Narrative
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US (TMUS) just put its Formula 1 regional partnership on full display in Las Vegas, using a dense 5G setup to support broadcast production, venue operations, payments and fan experiences across the Grand Prix. For investors watching T-Mobile US, the Formula 1 showcase lands against a trickier tape, with the share price at US$162.53 and a 7 day share price return that is down 4.97% following headlines about rising wireless competition and questions around future buyback capacity.

description: T-Mobile US, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides wireless communications services in the United States, Puerto Rico, and the United States Virgin Islands. The company offers voice, messaging, and data services to postpaid, prepaid, and wholesale and other services customers. It also provides wireless devices, including smartphones, wearables, tablets, home broadband gateways, headsets, and other mobile communication devices, as well as accessories; financing through equipment installment plans; reinsurance for device insurance policies and extended warranty contracts. The company offers services under the T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile brands through its owned and operated retail stores, customer care channels, national retailers, and its websites, as well as through T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile apps. It also sells devices to dealers and other third-party distributors for resale through independent third-party retail outlets and various third-party websites. It has 700 MHz wireless spectrum licenses. The company was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Bellevue, Washington. T-Mobile US, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom AG.
